title: objectql: engine.find logs `Find operation failed` at ERROR inside a catch that rethrows — the fourth member of #17052's class, scoped out on purpose
body:
`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`'s `find` door reports a failure it is about to
hand back to its caller at ERROR, through `reportFindFailure`. It is the same
shape #17052 repaired on the three write doors, and it is the one member of that
class #17052 deliberately did NOT repair.

⛔ Filed by the seat that landed #17052 (PR #17211), from the sweep that card
marked NOT MEASURED. It is scoped out of that PR on purpose — see "Why this is a
card and not a rider" below. **`domain:*` and `priority:*` are triage's to set** —
deliberately not set here.

## The site

`find`'s catch, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`:

```ts
} catch (e) {
    this.reportFindFailure(object, e);
    throw e;
}
```

and, one frame down in `reportFindFailure`, after the missing-table branch has
returned:

```ts
this.logger.error('Find operation failed', error as Error, { object });
```

The rethrow is the next statement, and it is the catch's only exit.

## The contract it violates

AGENTS.md, *Degradation log levels — `warn` vs `error`*, verbatim:

> **And a failure handed to the CALLER is not a degradation at all** — the third
> legal answer: a `catch` that answers `errorFromThrown(e, 400)`, or a batch
> whose contract IS a per-item outcome report, does not look normal from the
> outside — the requester was told. Do **not** bolt a `logger.error` onto such a
> site.

The requester was told: `e` is rethrown one line down, unmodified.

## Measured, in the #17052 sweep

An AST matcher over `packages/objectql/src` (145 files carrying a `catch`),
following same-file helper calls one frame and requiring the ERROR log to sit on
the same path as the rethrow, found exactly four members of the class:

| site | message | disposition |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `engine.ts` `insert` | `Insert operation failed` | repaired in #17052 |
| `engine.ts` `update` | `Update operation failed` | repaired in #17052 |
| `engine.ts` `delete` | `Delete operation failed` | repaired in #17052 |
| `engine.ts` `find` | `Find operation failed` | **this card** |

One further catch was discriminated out and is correct as it stands:
`hook-wrappers.ts` logs at ERROR only on the `onError:'log'` branch that
suppresses and returns, and logs nothing on its rethrow branch — there the
caller is genuinely not told.

## Why this is a card and not a rider on #17052

`reportFindFailure`'s level was set by a separate, recent ruling: the missing-table
demotion, whose docblock argues the non-benign branch stays `error` and weighs it
against the driver's own surviving `warn` line ("the driver already puts one
warn-level line per refusal in front of a reader, so a second would move this
noise rather than remove it"). That reasoning is about the READ path's own
duplicate-noise budget, which the write doors do not have. Overturning it is a
decision, not a repair, so it does not belong inside a card about the write doors.

#17052 did correct that docblock's now-false sentence about the write verbs
("`insert`/`update`/`delete` keep their unconditional `error`") and recorded the
open question there, but left the level itself untouched.

## What this card does NOT decide

⛔ It does not prescribe the level. The two facts a decision needs:

- The driver's own `warn` (`SqlDriver.backendStatementFault`) already carries the
  table, the dialect reason and the compiled statement for the refusal class,
  and `runtime/src/expected-read-refusal-noise.ts` documents it as where this
  class of fault is picked up. So a demotion here may cost less than it does on
  a write door.
- But `find`'s catch is reached by faults with no such sibling line
  (a connection drop, a permission denial, a query fault), and for those this
  entry is the only operator-facing copy.

## Not measured here

- ⛔ Whether the same shape exists outside `packages/objectql`. The #17052 sweep
  was scoped to that package by its dispatch; the matcher is general and the
  scan root is a one-line change.
- ⛔ Whether any consumer depends on the ERROR level of `Find operation failed`.
  The #17052 survey covered the three write messages only.
